bug_description.original: An out-of-bounds read occurs in libFLAC/bitreader.c.
bug_description.normalized: The staged FLAC witness reaches `frame_sync_` on a `skip_single_frame()` path and makes the decoder accept a candidate frame sync, after which `FLAC__bitreader_reset_read_crc16()` snapshots the current bitreader cursor into `crc16_offset` and `crc16_align`. A later bitreader clear reached through the same decoder object zeros `words`, `bytes`, `consumed_words`, and `consumed_bits`, but leaves those CRC fields untouched. In the staged vulnerable source, the decoder-side statement that performs this clear is `FLAC__stream_decoder_flush()` calling `FLAC__bitreader_clear()`; other public operations such as `FLAC__stream_decoder_reset()` and seek logic can reach that same flush internally, and the saved artifacts do not distinguish which path fired in this witness. On the final crashing `skip_single_frame()` resync, `FLAC__bitreader_read_raw_uint32()` exhausts the buffer again and `bitreader_read_from_client_()` calls `crc16_update_block_()`. Vulnerable `crc16_update_block_()` unconditionally executes `FLAC__crc16_update_words32(br->buffer + br->crc16_offset, br->consumed_words - br->crc16_offset, ...)`, so when the current `consumed_words` is still smaller than the stale `crc16_offset`, the unsigned subtraction wraps to a huge length. `FLAC__crc16_update_words32()` then dereferences `words[0]` / `words[1]` past `br->buffer`, and the staged MemorySanitizer trace reports `SEGV` caused by a READ at `src/libFLAC/crc.c:404`. Commit `c34c3459b514df02d922a882d406986e7f47afa4` fixes this exact bug by guarding the bulk CRC update with `if (br->consumed_words > br->crc16_offset)`.

source.description: First project-side statement that materializes attacker-controlled stream state used by the bug. After `frame_sync_` has already matched the leading `0xff`, this assignment records the second sync/header byte of a candidate frame and admits the parser into `read_frame_`, which immediately seeds CRC bookkeeping from the current bitreader cursor.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled stream bytes returned by `FLAC::Decoder::FuzzerStream::read_callback()` into the FLAC bitreader buffer. `frame_sync_` consumes them 8 bits at a time; the accepted `0xff`/`x` candidate sync pair is the direct input that leads to CRC state initialization.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.code:
crc = FLAC__crc16_table[7][crc >> 8               ] ^ FLAC__crc16_table[6][crc & 0xFF             ] ^
      FLAC__crc16_table[5][(words[0] >>  8) & 0xFF] ^ FLAC__crc16_table[4][ words[0]        & 0xFF] ^
      FLAC__crc16_table[3][ words[1] >> 24        ] ^ FLAC__crc16_table[2][(words[1] >> 16) & 0xFF] ^
      FLAC__crc16_table[1][(words[1] >>  8) & 0xFF] ^ FLAC__crc16_table[0][ words[1]        & 0xFF];
sink.description: MSan sink. The wrapped `len` and advanced `words` pointer from `crc16_update_block_()` make this CRC loop dereference past `br->buffer`, and the staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: SEGV` on a READ at line 404 in this expression.

root_cause.code: br->read_crc16 = FLAC__crc16_update_words32(br->buffer + br->crc16_offset, br->consumed_words - br->crc16_offset, br->read_crc16);
root_cause.description: Missing wraparound guard. This bulk CRC call assumes `consumed_words >= crc16_offset`, but `FLAC__bitreader_clear()` can zero `consumed_words` without resetting `crc16_offset`. When the current resync scan later consumes only a smaller number of words, the unsigned subtraction underflows and the CRC helper reads out of bounds. The fix adds the missing predicate `if (br->consumed_words > br->crc16_offset)` around this call.

tainted_value_origin.description: First concrete vulnerability-relevant state. CRC tracking snapshots the current bitreader cursor into `crc16_offset`; if `consumed_words` is later cleared independently, this saved offset becomes stale and is reused in the wrapped subtraction at the root cause.

parser_admitted.description: The attacker-controlled byte pair is accepted as a frame-sync candidate, so control leaves `SEARCH_FOR_FRAME_SYNC` and enters `read_frame_`, where CRC state is initialized from the current cursor.

evidence_limitations: The saved artifacts do not preserve which `read_frame_header_()` rejection branch or which public decoder method / internal path reached `FLAC__stream_decoder_flush()` before the crashing `skip_single_frame()` call.

The source-grounded fact is narrower and sufficient for closure: `FLAC__stream_decoder_flush()` calls `FLAC__bitreader_clear()`, and that clear zeros `consumed_words` without also resetting `crc16_offset`, so some path on the same decoder object must have reached that flush before the final crashing resync.

fine_trace.note: Source. After `frame_sync_` has already matched the first sync byte `0xff`, this statement records the attacker-controlled second sync/header byte and admits the parser into `READ_FRAME`. That control transfer is what causes `read_frame_()` to initialize CRC bookkeeping from the current cursor.

This call snapshots the current bitreader cursor into CRC state for the candidate frame: `crc16_offset` stores the current consumed whole-word count and `crc16_align` stores the bit offset inside the head word. Those fields persist until the next `crc16_update_block_()` and become the stale values later reused at the root cause.

A later clear on the same decoder object zeros the live buffer/consumption counters but does not touch `read_crc16`, `crc16_offset`, or `crc16_align`. In the staged vulnerable source, the decoder-side statement that performs this clear is `FLAC__stream_decoder_flush()` calling `FLAC__bitreader_clear()`, and other public operations such as `FLAC__stream_decoder_reset()` or seek logic can reach that same flush; the preserved artifacts do not distinguish which path occurred, but any such path leaves `crc16_offset` stale and potentially larger than the new `consumed_words`.

On the final crashing `skip_single_frame()` resync, repeated 8-bit reads eventually exhaust the post-clear buffer again and re-enter this refill loop. By then the scan has consumed at least one whole word after the clear, so `consumed_words` is positive again, but the preserved source-level stale state still allows it to remain smaller than the older `crc16_offset` from step 2.

Because the current resync scan has already consumed at least one whole word since the clear, refill takes this branch and invokes `crc16_update_block_()` before compacting and refilling the buffer. The stale CRC fields from step 2 survive into this call, so `crc16_update_block_()` now sees post-clear `consumed_words` together with a pre-clear `crc16_offset`.

fine_trace.code: br->read_crc16 = FLAC__crc16_update_words32(br->buffer + br->crc16_offset, br->consumed_words - br->crc16_offset, br->read_crc16);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The vulnerable code calls the bulk CRC helper without first proving `br->consumed_words > br->crc16_offset`. After step 3, the current `consumed_words` can still be smaller than the stale saved offset, so the unsigned subtraction wraps to a huge `len` and the helper starts from `br->buffer + br->crc16_offset`. The patch fixes this exact obligation by adding `if (br->consumed_words > br->crc16_offset)` around the call.

fine_trace.code:
crc = FLAC__crc16_table[7][crc >> 8               ] ^ FLAC__crc16_table[6][crc & 0xFF             ] ^
      FLAC__crc16_table[5][(words[0] >>  8) & 0xFF] ^ FLAC__crc16_table[4][ words[0]        & 0xFF] ^
      FLAC__crc16_table[3][ words[1] >> 24        ] ^ FLAC__crc16_table[2][(words[1] >> 16) & 0xFF] ^
      FLAC__crc16_table[1][(words[1] >>  8) & 0xFF] ^ FLAC__crc16_table[0][ words[1]        & 0xFF];
fine_trace.note: Sink. Step 6 passes an out-of-range `words` pointer and a wrapped `len`, so this loop body dereferences `words[0]` and `words[1]` beyond `br->buffer`. The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: SEGV on unknown address` caused by a READ at `src/libFLAC/crc.c:404:57` in this expression.

format.name: fuzzer_decoder datasource
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 133-byte datasource `poc` (sha256 `8423f0b8988996ec504a3951fd828a5832c6e30311081e745c5517ae2a7ae5cc`) interpreted by `fuzzer_decoder`'s `fuzzing::datasource::Datasource`. On one run of the same `FLAC::Decoder::FuzzerStream` object, the datasource must first supply stream bytes that make `frame_sync_()` accept a candidate frame sync so `FLAC__bitreader_reset_read_crc16()` seeds a nonzero `crc16_offset`, and it must also select a later decoder path that reaches `FLAC__stream_decoder_flush()` / `FLAC__bitreader_clear()` before the final crashing `skip_single_frame()` call. The final `skip_single_frame()` then has to rescan enough bytes that refill re-enters `crc16_update_block_()` with `0 < consumed_words < stale crc16_offset`, causing `consumed_words - crc16_offset` to wrap. The saved artifacts do not distinguish which public decoder method or internal path reached that flush, so this contract does not generalize beyond witnesses that reproduce that same stale-CRC-state relation on this fuzz target.
